title: Remove the dead chore art and --role-highlight, its only reader
body:
## Summary
apps/desktop/src/art/chore.tsx, chore.css and chore.test.tsx draw a picture nothing imports since b0d8d8b deleted the chore page and the field; removing them is blocked only by the sheet-users gate, because chore.tsx is the last reader of the --role-highlight token in styles/app.css.

## Description
b0d8d8b (2026-10-14, chores catalogue) removed `import ChoreArt from "@/art/chore"` and `artFor` from scenes/chores; since then `git grep` finds ChoreArt, ChoreArtBody, windowsFor, MAX_WINDOWS and `.chore-art` only inside apps/desktop/src/art/chore.* (211 + 20 + 51 lines). Deleting the three files kept `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint` at 0, but `src/styles/sheet-users.test.ts:76` went red: `--role-highlight` (apps/desktop/src/styles/app.css:64 and :111) is read by apps/desktop/src/art/chore.tsx:56 (TINTS) and by nothing else. The fix therefore needs the token removed from both themes in app.css, which is outside this round's paths (styles context), so the round reverted its attempt. Fixed looks like: the three art files deleted and `--role-highlight` dropped from both theme blocks, sheet-users green. The registry map cites apps/desktop/src/art/chore.tsx:15 as evidence for the motion subject; a /conform pass should re-anchor it (art/glyphs.tsx:7 says the same thing).

## Flow
- git grep -n "art/chore|ChoreArt|chore-art|windowsFor|MAX_WINDOWS" -- apps packages examples src tests scripts: zero hits outside art/chore.*
- git rm the three files: typecheck 0, lint 0, test 1 red (sheet-users: ["--role-highlight"] unread)
- remove --role-highlight from app.css dark and light blocks; re-run pnpm test: expected green

## Expected impact
Developers: 282 lines and one token that render nowhere stop being maintained and swept (this round read them in full). Could break: nothing at runtime (zero importers); a future chore drawing would be rebuilt from history.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - 282 dead lines and one dead token removed
Before: 3 files, 0 importers (grep above); --role-highlight read by 1 file, the dead one
After: 0 files; sheet-users green once the token goes (attempted: typecheck 0, lint 0, sheet-users red until app.css is edited)
Method: gate - zero-consumer grep and the real deletion run through all three desktop gates; the token edit is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: git rm apps/desktop/src/art/chore.{tsx,css,test.tsx}; drop --role-highlight from both theme blocks of apps/desktop/src/styles/app.css; pnpm typecheck, lint and test (sheet-users.test.ts must be green) from apps/desktop

title: A bell pose change snaps every tendril and the body to a new phase
body:
## Summary
Each pose sets a new `--pulse` and `--sway`, which changes `animation-duration` on running infinite animations; the browser keeps the elapsed time and recomputes progress, so the body squash and all nine tendrils jump in one frame, and leaving hearing or asking removes the ripples mid-expansion.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/bell/bell.css:16-18 set `--pulse` (5.5s rest, 1.6s working, 1.2s hearing, 2.2s asking) and `--sway`; bell.css:25 (`bell-pulse var(--pulse)`), :107 and :114 (sway durations divided by `--sway`) derive their durations from them. A CSS animation whose duration changes mid-flight keeps its current time and jumps to `time / newDuration`, so a pose flip is a discontinuity on every animated part at once. bell.css:63 runs the ripples only under hearing/asking; on any other pose the rule stops matching and both ripples vanish at whatever scale they had. This contradicts the bell's own promise that a pose change is eased (Bell.tsx:4-10 eases only the lean and the lit fade) and the motion golden path's continuity-across-change technique (animate the property that changed, never re-seat the whole surface). Fixed looks like: fixed base durations with the tempo applied as a playback rate on pose change (`Animation.updatePlaybackRate`, one call per pose change, not per frame), which preserves the current progress, and a ripple exit that finishes its current cycle (or fades on opacity) rather than being unset.

## Flow
- Surface scene, resting for 10 s, then a run starts: pose resting -> working
- body: progress 10/5.5 = 0.818 (scale about 0.995, 1.009) becomes 10/1.6 = 0.25 (about 1.023, 0.961): the dome's height drops ~5% in one frame (~10 px at size 420)
- tendril 0 sway: 5 s alternate at t=10 s is at -4deg; at 2.27 s it is 0.4 into a forward iteration, about -0.85deg: a 3deg snap at the root, more at the tip, on all nine at once
- a card is answered: asking -> resting; both ripple ellipses disappear mid-scale

## Expected impact
Everyone who watches her on Surface, Voice or Waking sees a twitch at every state change, which is exactly when they look. Measured as the progress jump per animated element across a pose flip. Could break: the perf:bell budget if the rate change is done per frame instead of once.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a pose change eases instead of twitching
Before: computed: body progress 0.818 -> 0.25 and tendril-0 rotation -4deg -> -0.85deg at a resting->working flip 10 s in; ripples removed mid-scale on 2 of 4 pose exits
After: predicted: progress continuous (jump 0) under updatePlaybackRate; ripples finish or fade
Method: simulation - the jump is computed from the keyframes and the spec's duration-change rule; measuring it needs a real browser, and this round's perf drive does not sample animation progress
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: extend scripts/perf-bell.drive.mjs: before and after each pose flip, read `getAnimations()` on .bell__body and each .bell__sway and record `effect.getComputedTiming().progress`; count elements whose progress jumps by more than 0.05 in one flip (Before: all of them; After: 0), with perf:bell still passing

title: The halo ignores the Calm choice; only OS reduced motion stills it
body:
## Summary
Every desktop surface reads the resolved `data-motion` that `lib/motion.ts` writes from the person's choice (system, calm, full), but the halo window only reads `prefers-reduced-motion` (halo.css:296, main.ts:34), so Calm leaves the overlay's travel, breathe and level chase running and Full cannot override an OS preference.

## Description
lib/motion.ts:9-15 makes the resolved choice the only thing a stylesheet reads, "so a person's choice and the OS's preference cannot disagree on screen". The halo page does not load the app's sheet or settings and its capability grants events only (src-tauri/src/halo.rs:15, capabilities/halo.json), so it cannot see the choice: apps/desktop/src/halo/halo.css:296 keys its still mode on the media query and apps/desktop/src/halo/main.ts:65 skips smoothing on `still.matches` only. The choice therefore has to arrive on the one wire the halo has: a `calm` field on HaloSignal (lib/halo-signal.ts:79, the Rust mirror RawSignal/Signal at src-tauri/src/halo.rs:78-92, lib/halo.ts signalOf), set by the producer from `resolveMotion(useSettings.motion, systemPrefersReduced())`, written by main.ts as `data-motion` on the root, with halo.css keyed on it. The Rust struct is outside this round's paths. Technique: loop-pause-governance (one merged pause signal) and reduced-motion-mechanics.

## Flow
- Settings -> Motion: Calm, OS reduced motion off
- hold the summon chord: Main and her window hold still; the halo's edges still chase the level at 60 fps; a run starts: the thinking traveller circles the screen; a card waits: the gate breathes
- the reverse: Motion: Full with the OS asking for less: the app moves, the halo stays still
- fix order: HaloSignal.calm + Rust mirror + wire test; producer sets it; main.ts writes data-motion; halo.css reduced block keyed on [data-motion="calm"]

## Expected impact
People who chose Calm (often for vestibular reasons) get full-screen motion at the edges of every monitor while talking to her. Measured as motion choices the halo honours. Could break: the Rust wire test and the halo's reduced look, both pinned by tests that would move with it.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the halo honours the same Calm choice as every other surface
Before: 1 of 3 choices honoured (system, via the media query); calm and full are ignored (halo.css:296, main.ts:34)
After: 3 of 3, pinned by a parseSignal test, a halo.css.test rule check and the Rust round-trip test
Method: probe - read every motion gate in the halo page (2: the media block and main.ts `still`), neither reads data-motion; the build needs the Rust struct, outside this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: halo/model.test.ts: parseSignal keeps a boolean `calm`; halo.css.test.ts: the still rules match `[data-motion="calm"]`; src-tauri halo.rs round-trip test with `calm`; lib/halo.test.ts: signalOf carries the resolved choice (0 of 3 cases pass before, 3 of 3 after)

title: Gate breathe and thinking traveller skip the edge fade and snap
body:
## Summary
Every steady edge opacity is scaled by `--live` so a phase fades in and out over 400 ms, but the gate's `breathe` keyframes set absolute opacities and the thinking traveller is `display: none` the moment the phase leaves, so the pink edges appear at 0.35 in one frame and the bright stretch vanishes in one frame.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/halo/halo.css:92 and :181 multiply edge opacity by `var(--live)`, and halo.css.test.ts pins that "every steady edge opacity is scaled by it". apps/desktop/src/halo/halo.css:237-247 animates `.edge` opacity 0.35 <-> 1 for the gate with no `--live` factor, so idle -> gate starts the breathe at 0.35 instantly (the window was just shown), and gate -> idle drops from the breathe's current value to the steady formula in one frame before fading. apps/desktop/src/halo/halo.css:183-184 shows the traveller only under thinking, so thinking -> idle removes it at once while the band under it is still fading. Fixed looks like: breathe keyframes written as `calc(0.35 * var(--live))` and `calc(1 * var(--live))` (or the breathe moved to an inner layer whose parent carries the fade), and the traveller hidden by opacity under the same fade. Whether WebView2 keeps a var()-dependent opacity animation on the compositor must be measured, which is why this is not built blind. Technique: continuity-across-change.

## Flow
- nothing is happening; a card arrives: the halos are shown and the pink edges pop in at 0.35, where every other phase fades in over 400 ms
- the card is answered while the breathe is at 1.0: the edges drop to 0.55 in one frame, then fade
- a run ends: the thinking stretch disappears in one frame mid-edge

## Expected impact
Anyone with a card waiting sees the one phase that pops instead of easing; measured as edge opacity steps over 0.2 in a single frame at a phase flip. Could break: a gate breathe that falls off the compositor would cost a main-thread frame per vsync for as long as a card waits.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the gate and thinking ornaments enter and leave on the halo's fade
Before: 2 of 4 non-idle phases (gate, thinking's traveller) bypass --live; 3 snaps per walked flip sequence above
After: predicted 0 snaps; breathe still composited (to be measured)
Method: simulation - read from halo.css; the compositing question needs a browser probe this round has no harness for (no halo perf scene)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a Playwright probe over halo.html?demo (or a perf-gate halo scene): sample `.edge` computed opacity every frame across idle->gate, gate->idle and thinking->idle and count single-frame steps > 0.2 (Before 3, After 0); during a steady gate, assert no main-thread animation frames (the perf gate's loopsPerFrame/idleFrameRequests)

title: Async athena_halo can fan two halo frames out in the wrong order
body:
## Summary
The producer fires `athena_halo` without awaiting, up to 30 times a second, and the command is `async`, which Tauri runs as a separate task per call; a level frame sent just before an idle frame can be emitted after it, leaving the overlays on speaking with the idle hide cancelled.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/lib/halo.ts:179 calls `deps.invoke(signal)` fire-and-forget on every change and every 34 ms level tick. apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/halo.rs:292 declares `pub async fn athena_halo`, which Tauri 2 spawns on the async runtime per invocation; on a multi-threaded runtime two tasks spawned back to back can run in either order. `signal` (halo.rs:260-267) bumps the generation on every frame, so a late `speaking` frame landing after `idle` both repaints the page as speaking (the page holds the caption while speaking, model.ts HOLDS) and invalidates the idle hide's generation: the halos stay up, on the last level, until the next change. The page has no sequence number to drop a stale frame. Fixed looks like: a synchronous command (`pub fn`, run in order on the main thread; the body never awaits) or a monotonically increasing `seq` on HaloSignal that the page and the hide timer ignore when stale. The command lives in desktop-shell-rust's paths.

## Flow
- she finishes speaking: the 34 ms loop sends speaking level 0.42, the voice store flips to idle and the producer sends idle within the same tick
- Tauri spawns two tasks; the idle task runs first: emit idle, schedule the 4.5 s hide
- the speaking task runs second: emit speaking, bump the generation: the page shows speaking with her caption held, and the hide no longer matches
- nothing else is sent at rest, so the halo stays up until the next turn

## Expected impact
Rare (two tasks microseconds apart) but sticky when it happens: an always-on-top glow and her last line left over every monitor. Measured as frames emitted out of send order. Could break: nothing if the command becomes sync; its body does no I/O.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - frames reach the overlays in the order they were sent
Before: ordering not guaranteed: 1 async command fed by fire-and-forget calls at up to 30 Hz (simulated, not reproduced)
After: predicted 0 reorderings with a sync command or a seq guard
Method: simulation - the interleaving is walked on halo.ts:179 and halo.rs:260-292; reproducing needs a Tauri runtime harness, and the command is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: either a Rust unit test over a pure `accept(seq)` guard (a frame with a lower seq than the last emitted is dropped) plus a TS model test that parseSignal/receive ignore a stale seq, or a Tauri mock-runtime test that invokes athena_halo twice back to back 1000 times and counts emits out of order (Before > 0 on a multi-thread runtime, After 0 with a sync command)

title: The bell and the halo disagree on whether a waiting card outranks a live turn
body:
## Summary
bell/pose.ts says its precedence "is the halo's", but the bell puts a waiting card above everything (asking) while the halo puts listening, speaking and any run above a card (gate last), so the two renderings of her state contradict each other whenever a card waits during a turn.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/bell/pose.ts:10-11: "Precedence is the halo's, for the same reason: what the person must act on wins over what she is doing"; pose.ts:30 returns asking first when cards > 0. apps/desktop/src/lib/halo-signal.ts:49-57: "Listening wins ... then her voice, then any work in flight, then a waiting card", and haloPhase returns gate only when nothing else is happening. Probed on the same states: a held key with one card -> bell asking, halo listening; a run in flight with two cards -> bell asking, halo thinking. Either the rule or the comment is wrong, and which order is right is a product call: the halo's reason (the person is talking and must see it) and the bell's (what needs the person wins) are both stated as intent.

## Flow
- a card waits; the person holds the summon chord
- Surface's bell shows asking (pink, ripples); every monitor's halo shows listening (pale cyan)
- decision: pick one order, make both functions follow it, and pin it with one parity test over the state product

## Expected impact
The person sees two different answers to "what is she doing" at the same moment. Measured as disagreeing states over the card-under-activity cases. Could break: whichever surface changes order changes what a person sees during a turn.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one precedence for her state across the bell and the halo
Before: 2 of 2 probed card-under-activity states disagree; the pose.ts comment asserts they agree
After: 0 of N once an order is chosen and pinned by a parity test
Method: probe - ran poseOf and haloPhase on the same two states by reading both functions; which order is correct is not measurable
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: Halo listening hue is no house role; the bell listens in another
body:
## Summary
halo.css says its hues are the house's roles, but `--halo-listen` (#a5f3fc) matches no token, while the bell's hearing pose uses `--role-external` (#87d0fb), so the person's own turn is drawn in two different colours.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/halo/halo.css:9-10: "The hues are the house's roles (styles/app.css): ... the person's turn is a paler cyan"; halo.css:17 `--halo-listen: #a5f3fc` has no counterpart in apps/desktop/src/styles/app.css. apps/desktop/src/bell/bell.css:17 colours the hearing pose with `--role-external` (#87d0fb dark). The other three halo hues are now pinned to their tokens (halo.css.test.ts); this one was left out because aligning it is a colour decision: make listening `--role-external` in both, or name a new role for the person's voice in app.css and use it in both.

## Flow
- hold the summon chord on Surface: the bell turns #87d0fb, the screen edges #a5f3fc
- decision: one hue for the person's turn, a token for it, and the halo copy pinned like the other three

## Expected impact
A visual-consistency gain for anyone who sees both at once (Surface open while speaking). Could break: the listening edge's contrast over light wallpapers if the darker role is chosen.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one colour for the person's turn
Before: 2 hues for listening (#a5f3fc halo, #87d0fb bell); 1 of 4 halo hues not a house role
After: 1 hue, 4 of 4 halo hues pinned
Method: probe - compared the two stylesheets' values; which hue is right is a design choice
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: Caption speaker label takes the phase colour, not the speaker's
body:
## Summary
`.caption .who` is coloured `var(--hue)`, the phase hue, not the speaker's, so the same "YOU" or "ATHENA" label changes colour as phases pass under a lingering line and reads as a different speaker.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/halo/halo.css:282 `color: var(--hue)`. The caption lingers 4 s after the phase leaves a hold (halo/model.ts CAPTION_LINGER_MS) and is held through thinking, so the label repaints with whatever phase comes next: "YOU" turns agent violet while she thinks about what you said, "ATHENA" turns human pink if a card lands during her linger, and at idle the hue resets to cyan after 400 ms (halo.css:84) under a still-visible label. A per-speaker colour (you = the person's hue, athena = her glow) would keep the label's meaning stable; whether the label should instead echo the phase is a design call.

## Flow
- speak a question: "YOU" in pale cyan; release: thinking, the same "YOU" turns violet
- she answers and a card is filed: "ATHENA" turns pink for the rest of the linger

## Expected impact
Anyone reading the caption: the who-label's colour stops meaning who. Could break: nothing structural; one CSS rule and a data attribute for who.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the speaker label's colour names the speaker
Before: label colour follows 5 phase hues; 2 walked sequences recolour a label under a still-visible line
After: 2 colours, one per speaker, constant for a line's life
Method: simulation - walked from model.ts and halo.css; whether the label should echo the phase is taste
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: The voice studio's 104 px bell draws its progress tendrils under a pixel wide
body:
## Summary
Tendril strokes are 1.4 (resting) and 2.8 (lit) in a 400-unit viewBox, so the studio rail's bell at 104 px draws them 0.36 px and 0.73 px wide, and the lit-or-not state that marks each finished step is below what a screen can show.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/bell/bell.css:79 `stroke-width: 1.4` with stroke-opacity 0.3 and bell.css:87 `stroke-width: 2.8` for the lit overlay, in Bell.tsx's 400x420 viewBox. apps/desktop/src/scenes/voice/studio.tsx:168-177 gives the rail's bell three tendrils (engine, voice, ears), lit as each step is done, at `size={104}`: 1.4 x 104 / 400 = 0.36 px, 2.8 x 104 / 400 = 0.73 px. On Surface (420) the same strokes are 1.47 and 2.94 px. A `vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke` on the tendril paths would keep ~1.4/2.8 px at every size (and change the 420 px bell by under 0.1 px), but how heavy that reads at 104 px needs eyes on the real window.

## Flow
- open Voice -> studio; finish the engine step
- the rail's bell lights its first tendril: a 0.73 px stroke next to a 0.36 px one at 0.3 opacity

## Expected impact
People in the studio: the bell's progress cue becomes legible. Could break: the large bells' look if the fix is not size-neutral (it nearly is).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the studio bell's tendrils are visible at the size it is drawn
Before: 0.36 px resting and 0.73 px lit at 104 px (computed from the CSS and the size prop)
After: about 1.4 px and 2.8 px with non-scaling strokes (computed); legibility to be judged on screen
Method: probe - the widths are arithmetic on the real stylesheet and call site; whether the fix looks right needs the window
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
